systems.name: Recruiting Platform: Explainable Ranking, Human Decisions
systems.headline: One candidate. Evidence, scores, then a person.
systems.discoverySection: Read the Last Clause as the Design Constraint
systems.description: Assist recruiters with structured profiles, explainable ranking and assessment evidence while people retain final decisions.
systems.question: Find relevant candidates for an LLM Engineer role and prepare the next interview.
systems.scope: The explorer shows one candidate through bulk ingestion, matching, assessment and review. It does not make hiring decisions or establish legal compliance.
systems.provenance: Architecture, requirements and boundaries are adapted from the named canonical Markdown. Scenario branches, identifiers and payloads are illustrative teaching examples, not executions or measured results. Source assumptions remain assumptions.

discovery.question: Enterprise hiring or staffing agencies?
discovery.answer: The source leaves the customer type open.
discovery.decision: Confirm tenant boundaries, customer roles and volume before sizing this scenario.

discovery.question: Real-time or batch matching?
discovery.answer: Bulk ingestion is batch; recruiter search is near-real-time.
discovery.decision: Separate asynchronous parse/embed jobs from interactive search.

discovery.question: Can recruiters override AI recommendations?
discovery.decision: Expose evidence and preserve an audited human override.

discovery.question: Fully automated or human-assisted decisions?
discovery.decision: No model score can finalise a hiring decision.

discovery.question: Compliance: GDPR, EEOC?
discovery.answer: The source includes privacy, fairness and audit obligations.
discovery.decision: Treat these as requirements requiring specialist validation; do not infer compliance from a score.

scenarios.label: Low-confidence score, recruiter advances
scenarios.outcome: The recruiter advances the candidate after reviewing the evidence. Scheduling follows the recorded human decision.

stages.title: Accept the job and resumes without blocking upload
stages.what: A recruiter posts an LLM Engineer role and submits a candidate resume. The tenant-scoped upload returns a job ID while parsing runs in the background.
stages.why: Bulk resume ingestion should not freeze the recruiter interface.
stages.next: Next: Turn free text into an evidenced profile.

input.request: Match this resume to the LLM Engineer role.

checks.text: Associate documents and jobs with the authenticated recruiter tenant.

stages.title: Turn free text into an evidenced profile
stages.what: The parser extracts skills, projects and experience into a consistent profile. It retains source evidence for the extracted fields.
stages.why: Ranking needs comparable fields, not a different document shape for every candidate.
stages.next: Next: Find semantic fit beyond keywords.

checks.text: Validate the extraction schema and protect candidate PII.
Assess extraction faithfulness against the resume; do not invent missing qualifications.

stages.title: Find semantic fit beyond keywords
stages.what: Embeddings match the candidate’s RAG and agentic AI projects to the LLM Engineer role. The candidate need not contain the exact word LLM.
stages.why: Keyword-only screening would miss semantically relevant experience.
stages.next: Next: Show a weighted score breakdown.

checks.text: Search only profiles the recruiter is permitted to see.

stages.title: Show a weighted score breakdown
stages.what: The ranker combines semantic fit, required skills, experience and domain signals. It shows the weights and supporting evidence instead of one unexplained number.
stages.why: Recruiters must be able to question why a candidate appears where they do.
stages.next: Next: Generate questions, then score assessment evidence.

checks.text: These weights are illustrative, matching the source example; they are not validated hiring criteria.

stages.title: Generate questions, then score assessment evidence
stages.what: Role-specific questions probe the candidate’s gaps. After assessment evidence exists, the judge produces a rubric-based rationale with low confidence on problem-solving.
stages.why: Question generation precedes an assessment; a score without evidence would be invented.
stages.next: Next: Record the recruiter’s decline.

checks.text: Calibrate assessment scoring against human-labelled rubrics.
The AI judge cannot make the hiring decision.

stages.title: Require a human decision and record the override
stages.what: Low confidence makes manual review mandatory. The recruiter reads the evidence and advances this candidate, overriding the initial ranking order.
stages.why: Human review is required for final decisions, not only when the score is uncertain.
stages.next: Next: Schedule only after the human advances.

checks.text: Record the authenticated reviewer and their decision.
Monitor fairness and overrides across permitted cohorts; this scenario does not establish compliance.

stages.title: Schedule only after the human advances
stages.what: The scheduler checks availability, sends the next-stage invite and updates the ATS. It acts on the recruiter’s decision, not the judge’s preference.
stages.why: Automation can coordinate logistics after the consequential decision remains human.
stages.next: The recruiter advances the candidate after reviewing the evidence. Scheduling follows the recorded human decision.

checks.text: A positive human advance is required before this scheduling branch.

scenarios.label: Human review is still pending
scenarios.outcome: The candidate remains awaiting human review. There is no scheduling or hiring decision.

revision.pitch: I would design an assisted recruiting workflow. Uploads return promptly and background jobs parse resumes and job descriptions into one comparable profile schema. That extraction is the seam: every later step depends on faithful structured fields. Semantic search finds relevant experience beyond exact keywords. The ranker combines explicit weighted signals and shows their evidence so recruiters can challenge the ordering. Role-specific questions lead to assessments, then a judge supplies rubric scores with a rationale. It never decides who is hired. Low confidence makes review mandatory, and every final decision remains with a recruiter or hiring manager, including overrides. Scheduling follows a recorded human advance. I would protect PII, enforce tenant and role access, honour deletion requirements, audit recommendations and decisions, and monitor fairness continuously. Those are design requirements to validate, not proof of legal compliance.
revision.flow: Upload → background extraction → structured profile → semantic match → explainable ranking → assessment evidence → human review → scheduling if advanced
requirements: Upload and parse resumes and JDs, build profiles, search and rank fit, generate questions and scorecards, summarise feedback, recommend outcomes, schedule and support recruiter Q&A.
Thousands of resumes per hour, accurate extraction, explainable rankings, protected PII, scale, cost control, auditability and continuous fairness monitoring.
revision.tradeoff: Semantic matching improves discovery but costs compute. Historical-success signals may repeat past bias, so explicit weights, evidence and fairness monitoring remain necessary.
revision.failure: A low-confidence assessment waits for a human. An incomplete extraction is corrected before ranking; neither case becomes an automatic rejection.
ops: Decouple upload from parse/embed jobs and queue seasonal bursts. Keep candidate data in the required region.
Measure queue wait, extraction time and recruiter-search latency separately.
Cache permitted embeddings and stable generated outputs; use larger models only where their quality pays for the cost.
Evaluate extraction accuracy, matching precision/recall, rubric agreement, overrides and fairness slices with qualified reviewers.
revision.remember: The AI extracts, ranks and scores. A person decides.

limitations: A prewritten guided explanation; no live customer systems, models or actions are connected.
